subject: Dedicated capacity – SKU prioritization & runway plan for CrescentAI
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Liu <michael.liu@crescentai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity – SKU prioritization & runway plan for CrescentAI

Michael — thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a pragmatic SKU prioritization and 12-month runway estimate that balances latency SLAs, per-token unit economics, and headroom for bursty growth. Attached is the capacity model (CrescentAI_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a short one-pager (sku_tradeoff_onepager.pdf).

Summary recommendations (high level):
- H100 (8x80GB slots): Reserve for long-context and low-latency paths where you cannot tolerate sampling variance — expected to serve ~10% of traffic (preview + summarization with 50k+ context).
- A100 (4x40GB slots): Primary workhorse for sustained throughput and medium-context models; good for batched reranking and high-QPS normalized workloads.
- L4 (16GB): Cost-effective for chat/short prompt inference and fine-tuned small models used in many low-cost interactive surfaces; good as hedged overflow and for embedding workloads.

Sizing sketch (initial commit):
- Baseline traffic: 300 RPS average, 1.5M tokens/day.
- Long-context share (50k+ tokens): ~10% of requests but ~35% of tokens — allocate 6 H100 slots to meet 99th pct latency target at current QPS with x2 burst headroom.
- Sustained medium-context: allocate 12 A100 slots sized for batching; expected to handle 70% of token volume with better unit cost per token.
- Low-cost inference / embeddings: 8 L4 slots for cheap, scale-out capacity and embedding throughput.

Runway & headroom: the attached model includes 6, 12, 8 slots as the committed footprint with an ops-backed burst pool (on-demand) up to 30% extra capacity for holiday/spike scenarios. We show simple cost curves with quantization options to drop A100 needs by ~20% if you adopt INT8 for certain models.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: start with a 10% traffic split to the Dedicated capacity for a single use-case (document search) and measure token-level latency / failure rates for 2 weeks.
- Fallbacks: prefer L4 for cold-starts and implement model-variant routing so requests degrade to cheaper A100-quantized variants when H100 is saturated.
- Observability: we recommend per-route token-level tracing and a cost dashboard tied to each model version — sample dashboards are in the one-pager.

Next steps: can you confirm procurement timing & target commit (monthly vs annual)? If procurement prefers a smaller initial commit we can reduce H100 slots to 4 and rely more heavily on burst for the first quarter. Jordan — looping you for any ops constraints I missed.

— Naomi

Michael — good questions. Short answers below, and I also attached a small fidelity checklist you can run against ~20 eval prompts to validate quantized variants.

1) Latency targets: H100 sizing is targeting p50 ~60ms, p95 ~220ms, p99 ~400ms for the long-context summarization path (these include decoding time but exclude network egress). A100 batch paths expect p95 ~350ms at peak when relying on batching; individual interactive queries will be higher if unbatched.

2) Burst headroom: the 2x factor is conservative and based on a mix of historical customer telemetry (spike multipliers between 1.3–1.8) and a buffer for black-swan events. We modeled scenarios with 1.5x and 2.5x to show cost vs SLA tradeoffs; the spreadsheet has those sheets.

3) Quantization fidelity: INT8/A4B quantized A100 variants typically preserve ROUGE/BLEU-like scores within ~2–4% for contrastive summarization tasks we tested. For your specific summarizer we recommend running the attached 20-case checklist; if some prompts fall outside thresholds we can selectively keep H100 for those flows while serving the rest on quantized A100.

Jordan — quick ops question: do you see any infra limits on a mixed H100/A100/L4 Dedicated pool for Crescent's preferred cloud region (us-west-2)? If so flag what we should change in the commitment.

— Naomi

Looping in ops notes. We can support a mixed pool in us-west-2 without special network changes but a few call-outs: 
- H100 availability: limited pods in the preferred AZs; recommend a multi-AZ placement to meet the p99 latency SLA and avoid noisy-neighbor placement risk. This increases networking egress and cross-AZ costs ~3–5%.
- Boot time / cold-start: H100 model load times for very large context models can be 30–90s; recommend pre-warming and a small cache of hot replicas (included in the sizing workbook).
- L4 burst scaling: fine to autoscale aggressively, but ensure quota for concurrent L4 launches in account is increased before go-live.
- Contracting: from an ops standpoint, a 6-month ramp (commit to 70% in month 1, 85% month 3, 100% month 6) gives us flexibility to reserve fewer H100 initially and add A100s as traffic patterns stabilize.

Dev — full cost / ops runbook is ready; Naomi and I can present to Crescent procurement next week.
